title: E2F4 gene therapy reverses established synaptic and cognitive deficits and remodels learning-associated signaling in Alzheimer's disease mice
authors: Sanchez-Puelles, C.; Hernandez-Vivanco, A.; Grieco, A.; Camacho-Olmos, I.; Montero-Calle, A.; Lopez-Sanchez, N.; Fraj-Cebrian, A.; Garrido-Garcia, A.; Cano-Daganzo, V.; Lozano-Urena, A.; Valdes-Lora, L.; Barderas, R.; Perea, G.; Pascual-Leone, A.; Frade, J. M.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes progressive synaptic dysfunction, neurodegeneration, and cognitive decline, yet strategies capable of reversing established deficits remain limited. Here, we show that neuronal expression of a p38MAPK phosphorylation-resistant human E2F4 variant (hE2F4DN), delivered by adeno-associated virus, restores hippocampal long-term potentiation and memory in homozygous 5xFAD mice after functional impairment is established. Treatment also reduces amyloid-{beta} and phospho-tau pathology and prevents hippocampal neuronal loss. Integrated proteomic and phosphoproteomic analyses reveal remodeling of metabolic, redox, neuroimmune, synaptic-vesicle, and GSK3{beta}-associated signaling pathways. Following contextual fear conditioning, hE2F4DN-treated mice exhibit broader learning-associated synaptic proteomic signatures and distinct phosphoregulatory responses involving synaptic machinery. These findings demonstrate that E2F4 gene therapy can reverse established synaptic and cognitive deficits while preserving neuronal integrity and reshaping molecular responses to learning, identifying E2F4 phosphorylation as a potential therapeutic target for advanced AD states.

title: Is the Bitter Lesson coming to genomic prediction? An untuned tabular foundation model matches or beats specialized methods
abstract: Genomic prediction (GP) is dominated by models designed around assumptions about how genetic variation affects phenotypes. Here we asked how well a general-purpose pretrained tabular foundation model called TabPFN-3.5 does with no genetics-specific modeling and no tuning when given marker genotypes directly. We benchmarked TabPFN-3.5 using a published comparison of 18 GP methods on 18 traits in six plant species. Against the published means, TabPFN-3.5 ranked first on 11 of 18 traits and had the best median rank. Because the published benchmark did not identify its test sets, we reran GBLUP, RKHS and elastic-net models on the same splits as TabPFN-3.5. Against the best of these, TabPFN-3.5 was significantly behind on only one trait, spruce wood density, and ahead on 12 of 18, with significant gains on all three soybean traits and rice flowering time. In the soybean panel, which had the largest number of lines, its advantage was clearest. In leave-families-out cross-validation, where models were trained on some soybean families and used to predict lines from other families withheld from training, every model lost accuracy and TabPFN-3.5 performed on par with GBLUP and RKHS. That a general-purpose learner matches or exceeds decades of specialized GP models is consistent with Sutton's Bitter Lesson, which holds that methods that scale with computation eventually overtake those built on human knowledge of the domain.

title: Primate Saccade Rhythmicity
authors: Näher, T.; Zhang, Y.; Spadacenta, S.; Pandinelli, M.; Bastian, L.; Thier, P.; Hafed, Z. M.; Fries, P.
abstract: Rhythmic sampling is a hallmark of many sensory systems across diverse organisms. In primate vision, rapid foveating eye movements repetitively sample the visual environment at a rate of approximately 4 Hz. Yet, the observed inter-saccadic interval distributions might equally well be produced by a non-rhythmic stochastic process as by a - putatively variable- rhythmic generator. This raises the fundamental question whether primate visual sampling differs from the numerous examples of rhythmic sampling strategies exhibited across sensory modalities and species. Here, using experiments in humans, macaques, and a marmoset, as well as statistical approaches adopted from studies of temporal structure in neuronal spiking patterns, we show that primate saccade generation is unambiguously rooted in a rhythmic source. This finding was remarkably consistent across the three primate species despite their significant evolutionary distance. Importantly, we find that saccade rate undergoes smooth, slow fluctuations on the scale of seconds, and accounting for those rate fluctuations was crucial for revealing the true degree of saccade rhythmicity. Thus, exact saccade timing is determined by an interaction between the slow saccade-rate fluctuations and the more temporally-local rhythmic generator. This demonstration of rhythmicity in overt oculomotor sampling behavior provides a link to the fundamentally rhythmic nature of many central perceptual and cognitive processes, and places primate saccadic sampling into the large family of rhythmic active sampling behaviors.

title: EPHB2 promotes long-range axon extension and its variants cause callosal dysgenesis
authors: Park, S. S.; Nagy, G. N.; Perez Ferrer, I.; Coca, Y.; Herrera, M.; Kahwaji, C.; Zhang, X. B.; Liu, L.; Kolluru, S.; Neira, M.; Kerdjemil, Y.; Palombo, F.; La Morgia, C.; Caporali, L.; Carelli, V.; Waisfisz, Q.; Elting, M. W.; Houge, G. D.; Gradek, G. A.; Tveitnes, D.; Sheridan, E. G.; Prescott, K.; Redman, M.; Imam, A.; Ostergaard, P.; Anderson, K.; Weaver, D. D.; Schaefer, E.; Laugel, V.; Gan-Or, Z.; Dalva, M. B.; Depienne, C.; Jones, E. Y.; Herrera, E.; Kania, A.
abstract: The corpus callosum (CC) is the largest fibre tract connecting the cerebral hemispheres, essential for integrating neural activity across large-scale brain networks. Accordingly, abnormal CC development is associated with diverse neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders. Callosal projection neurons (CPNs) of the cortex form the CC by extending long-range axons to the contralateral hemisphere; however, the mechanisms that sustain axon elongation over such remarkable distances remain poorly understood. Here we show that variants in the human gene EPHB2, which encodes a tyrosine kinase receptor regulating nervous system development and implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders, cause CC dysgenesis. We characterise variant- specific effects on EPHB2 signalling and demonstrate that variants identified in individuals with distinct CC morphologies differentially alter CPN axon outgrowth and integration in vivo. We further show that EphB2 has a cell-autonomous, ligand-independent function in promoting CPN axon outgrowth by spatially organising actomyosin at axonal growth cones. These findings reveal a previously unrecognised role for EphB2 in promoting long-range axon extension and provide the first evidence that EPHB2 variants cause CC dysgenesis in humans. More broadly, our study links molecular variation in EPHB2 to individualised abnormalities in brain connectivity and provides a framework for understanding how heterogeneous circuit-level phenotypes arise in neurodevelopmental disorders.

title: Do altered neural responses during self-reflection converge across psychiatric disorders? A systematic review and meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies
authors: Zhu, S.; Yan, W.-J.; Chuan-Peng, H.
abstract: Altered neural responses during self-reflection have been reported across psychiatric disorders, but it is unknown whether there exist common brain regions across studies. To fill the gap, we conducted a systematic review and coordinate-based activation likelihood estimation (ALE) meta-analysis of task-based neuroimaging studies. Through systematic literature search and article screening, we identified 36 studies across 8 diagnostic categories, of which 25 studies were eligible for the ALE meta-analysis. Qualitatively, these studies revealed altered neural response among psychiatric disorders in brain regions include cortical midline and lateral association regions. ALE analyses were conducted separately for self-versus other and self-versus control contrasts, the former identified convergence in the right anterior cingulate cortex (ACC), and the latter found converged activation in the left middle frontal gyrus (MFG). These findings revealed a broad interest in neural response to self-evaluation but unevenly distributed studies across psychiatric disorders, and the available results only provided weak evidence of spatial convergence for altered neural response across psychiatric disorders.

title: Mathematical model for visual cortical development based on molecular mechanisms underlying the generation and elimination of dendritic spines
abstract: In the developing brain, neural circuits are elaborated by the activity-dependent rewiring of synaptic connections. The current view of synaptic rewiring in early development is that filopodia spontaneously generated along dendrites transform into spines by establishing contacts with neighboring axonal boutons to form synapses whereas spines of inappropriate synapses are eliminated in an activity-dependent manner. In this theoretical study, we mainly focus on the processes of spine generation, maturation, and elimination to build a mathematical model of synaptic rewiring, incorporating experimental findings on actin polymerization and depolymerization under the activation of Rho-GTPases mediated by the binding of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) to neurotrophin receptors such as tropomyosin kinase receptor B (TrkB) and the low-affinity-nerve growth factor receptor (p75NTR). TrkB receptors are dephosphorylated by chondroitin sulphate proteoglycans (CSPGs) mediated by protein-tyrosine phosphatase {sigma} (PTP{sigma} in an age-dependent manner. The model describes the generation or elimination of dendritic spines of visual cortical neurons under actin polymerization and depolymerization to establish appropriate synaptic contacts on afferent fibers of cells in the lateral geniculate nucleus. The simulations based on the model reproduced not only simple-cell-like receptive fields and orientation-direction maps but also a characteristic profile of the total number of synapses, which shows an early increase and a delayed decrease during the critical period. It is also demonstrated that the formation of direction selectivity is delayed behind the formation of orientation selectivity, which is likely promoted by the pruning of inappropriate synapses.

title: Unravelling the hidden diversity of the monkfish Lophius gastrophysus using integrative taxonomy
authors: D'Elia, A. K. P.; Soares, L. M. M.; Henning, F.; Sole-Cava, A. M.
abstract: The monkfish Lophius gastrophysus is a commercially exploited demersal species distributed along the continental shelf and slope of the western Atlantic Ocean. Like other anglerfish species, L. gastrophysus has a pelagic larval stage that can facilitate dispersal by oceanic currents (Farina et al., 2008). It is considered the most widely distributed species in the genus, spanning more than 10,000 km of the western Atlantic Coast, from North Carolina to Argentina. Previous morphological analyses based on a limited set of traits suggested that L. gastrophysus may comprise two distinct species. We tested this hypothesis by combining molecular and morphometric data. Sequence data were obtained from 38 L. gastrophysus individuals collected from Northern and Southern American populations. We also used a subset of 13 specimens for geometric morphometrics. Phylogenetic analyses and automatic species delimitation methods consistently distinguished Northern and Southern Atlantic L. gastrophysus as separate clades, and geometric morphometrics supported the same split. The congruence among geographic, molecular, and morphometric data indicates that L. gastrophysus harbours two distinct lineages, highlighting the need for a formal taxonomic revision and separate fisheries management of northern and southern Atlantic populations.

title: Centromere divergence and allopolyploidy reshape carnivorous sundew genomes
authors: Avila Robledillo, L.; Fukushima, K.; Salojarvi, J.; Marques, A.; Albert, V. A.
abstract: Centromeres are essential for chromosome function, yet how contrasting centromere architectures shape polyploid genome evolution and plant diversification remains unresolved. In monocentric chromosomes, centromeric activity is restricted to one chromosomal region; in holocentric chromosomes, it is distributed along the chromosome length. Hybridization followed by genome doubling can place chromosome sets with different centromeres, repeat complements, and rearrangement histories in the same nucleus. We examined whether such genomic mergers are associated with later chromosome restructuring in carnivorous Caryophyllales, focusing on chromosome-scale assemblies of putatively holocentric Drosera regia and monocentric D. capensis. The two sundews retain broad syntenic continuity and related polyploid ancestry, but their present genomes differ sharply. D. regia preserves several ancestral chromosomal fusions and dispersed candidate centromere-associated satellite repeats, whereas D. capensis has stronger internal duplication, extensive rearrangement, and localized centromeres. Phylogenomic and structural analyses suggest a reticulate evolutionary history for D. regia, with part of its genome showing preferential structural affinity to the Venus flytrap lineage. Whereas D. regia exhibits threefold syntenic depth consistent with hexaploidy, D. capensis exhibits sixfold depth consistent with dodecaploidy, and structural comparisons do not support simple doubling of the extant D. regia-like architecture. Repeat profiling across a broad sample of Drosera also shows rapid turnover and species-level differences in centromere-associated DNA. These results place centromere organization alongside polyploid history and chromosome restructuring as a major axis of genome evolution in sundews.

title: CLASSIFICATION OF PROKARYOTIC DNA METHYLTRANSFERASES BY CATALYTIC DOMAIN TOPOLOGY
abstract: Prokaryotic DNA methyltransferases (MTases) are essential enzymes that play a crucial role in restriction-modification systems, preventing the degradation of self DNA by restriction enzymes. In addition, they contribute to the regulation of gene expression, DNA repair, DNA replication, and other processes. Here, we propose a novel classification of prokaryotic MTases based on the 3D topology of the catalytic domain, which addresses the limitations of the previous scheme developed by Malone and Bujnicki. The latter, which grouped MTases into categories such as , {beta}, {gamma}, etc., has been in use for over 20 years. We identified seven structural classes (A-G) of MTases by analyzing 38 experimentally determined 3D structures and several AlphaFold-predicted models, and validated the classification against all reviewed DNA MTases from Swiss-Prot. The catalytic domains of each class exhibit homology not only in structure but also in conserved motifs. Our classification system provides a framework for understanding the diversity and evolution of prokaryotic DNA MTases, with applications in genomic annotation and evolutionary studies.

title: ISdetector: precise mapping of insertion sequences and associated structural variations from short-read sequencing data
authors: Zhou, Y.; Lu, B.; Zhao, Y.
abstract: Motivation. Repetitive insertion sequences (ISs) and adjacent structural variants (SVs) complicate precise mapping from bacte-rial short reads. Accurate insertion coordinates are important for studying genome evolution and tracking transmission. Results. ISdetector constructs IS-specific references with target copies removed and clusters soft-clipped reads to pinpoint insertion sites. On simulated genomes, it had higher recall and F1 score than ISMapper and MGEFinder. On 19 Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes, it achieved the highest high-confidence F1 score (0.86). On five Shigella sonnei genomes, it performed comparably to ISMapper (F1 score 0.85). It detected 81 of 105 IS6110 copies with associated SVs or complex events, versus 41 (ISMapper) and 12 (MGEFinder). With four threads, it outpaced both comparators at any thread count. Availability and Implementation. ISdetector is implemented in Python and the archived release are available at https://github.com/carolynzy/ISdetector/releases/tag/v1.1.0 .

title: Inferring single-cell gene expression profiles from multicellular spatial transcriptomics data with st2sc
authors: Lee, Y. J.; Shah, S.; Mantrala, S.; Lugo-Martinez, J.
abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables the quantitative measurement of gene expression within tissue sections but is currently limited in spatial resolution, as each spot aggregates signals from multiple cells. Recovering single-cell gene expression profiles from these multicellular measurements requires two steps: explicit identification of individual cells and accurate estimation of per-gene expression. While existing methods have demonstrated the feasibility of recovering single-cell expression profiles, accurately estimating gene-level expression for individual cells remains an important challenge. To address this challenge, we propose st2sc (Spatial Transcriptomics to Single-Cell), an end-to-end framework for inferring single-cell gene profiles from multicellular ST data. st2sc introduces a novel Attention Gradient Flow Tracking (AGFT) algorithm that extracts attention maps from a Vision-Gene Transformer to identify candidate cell instances without predefined background constraints. The detected instances are then used by a set of regressors trained under a multiple-instance, multiple-target regression setting to predict precise single-cell gene expression counts. Comprehensive evaluations on synthetic and Visium-like datasets demonstrate that st2sc significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accurately segmenting cellular instances and predicting gene counts. The method can further resolve contested 2um bin in Visium HD. Application to human IPF lung showed the model can recover the subtype marker level analysis. This advancement further improves single-cell resolution analysis in spatial transcriptomics, facilitating more accurate downstream biological analyses.

title: DNA methylation assigns sequencing reads to closely related bacterial strains when their sequence cannot
abstract: Clinical and public-health questions often concern strains rather than species, yet co-resident strains of one species can be so closely related that a single long read carries no sequence difference between them. We measured how often this happens in 639 pairs of isolates of Enterococcus faecium, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Listeria monocytogenes and Staphylococcus aureus sequenced on one nanopore platform. Among the 297 pairs above 99% average nucleotide identity (ANI), 40.37% of read placements (a read counted against one strain's genome) carried no sequence difference between the two strains, and above 99.9% ANI about three quarters did. Strains of one species also differ in the DNA motifs they methylate. Our method, Epilect, assigns single nanopore reads to strains from the basecaller's methylation calls, given a methylation profile for each strain, and declines to call when the evidence is weak. In the pairs above 99% ANI it correctly assigned 21.8% of the read placements that sequence could not place, at a precision of 0.959. In computational mixtures of 65 pairs of distinct strains at or above 99.5% ANI that were predicted to differ in methylation, its per-read F1 score exceeded that of the best of three sequence-based read-phasing tools by 0.25 (95% CI 0.08 to 0.37); where equally related strains were predicted to share a methylome, the comparison reversed. DNA methylation therefore supplies strain evidence on reads whose sequence carries none, and whether it will do so for a given pair of strains can be estimated before sequencing.

title: Point mutations in the FimH lectin domain: predicted folding stability versus conformational dynamics for R60P, Q133K and Y137A
authors: Navas Passos, J. A.; Pereira Tapia, A.; Velez Duncan, C.; Alviz Amador, A.
abstract: Background. The adhesin FimH attaches uropathogenic Escherichia coli to the urinary epithelium through a force-regulated catch-bond that single lectin-domain substitutions can modulate. How such substitutions reshape the dynamics of the isolated lectin domain, and whether stability predictors anticipate them, is unclear. Methods. We compared the wild-type (WT) lectin domain (PDB 4XO8, apo) with R60P, Y137A and Q133K, using three 500 ns molecular dynamics (MD) replicates per system (6 microseconds total) and three folding-stability predictors (FoldX, a Cartesian-ddG-type Rosetta protocol, ERIS-2). The replicate was the unit of analysis (n = 3), with 95% confidence intervals and a WT replicate-to-replicate control. Results. FoldX and ERIS-2 ranked the variants consistently, R60P most destabilising and Q133K neutral; the Rosetta value for Q133K was anomalously high. All systems stayed folded. R60P gave the only reproduced local change, loss of beta-strand structure at residues 60-61 and of three local hydrogen bonds. Y137A did not bring Thr158 into the pocket, and the Q133K Gln133-Asp54 polar contact became a Lys133-Asp54 salt bridge. In the principal-component landscape, departures from the WT region came from individual replicates (Y137A replicate 1; Q133K replicates 2-3), not a systematic shift. Conclusions. A substitution perturbs local structure most clearly when it breaks a beta-strand (R60P), and the stability predictions and dynamics together give a consistent ranking of the variants, including the first dynamic characterisation of Q133K. The results characterise the apo lectin domain and give a reproducible basis for interpreting FimH mutations, not for inferring affinity. Keywords: FimH; lectin domain; point mutations; molecular dynamics; folding stability ({Delta}{Delta}G); protein stability prediction; principal component analysis; urinary tract infection.

title: A Rare Constitutional Centromeric Expansion of Chromosome 1 in a Phenotypically Normal Individual: A Comprehensive Cytogenetic Study
authors: Shirsath, K. B.; Desai, U. N.; Notnani, A.; Chaurasia, R. K.; Bhat, N. N.; Khan, A.
abstract: Constitutional centromeric heteromorphisms are uncommon chromosomal variants that may complicate cytogenetic interpretation. We report a constitutional enlargement of the centromeric region of one chromosome 1 homologue identified incidentally during biological dose estimation in a suspected occupationally exposed individual. Conventional cytogenetics, pancentromeric fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), and multiplex FISH confirmed the variant and excluded cryptic chromosomal rearrangements. Analysis of 500 metaphases revealed no dicentric chromosomes. Quantitative assessment demonstrated a centromere to chromosome length ratio of 0.314 plus/minus 0.019 for the enlarged homologue compared with 0.169 plus/minus 0.019 for the unaffected homologue and 0.161 to 0.186 in controls, representing an approximately 1.86 fold increase (t = 28.4, p < 0.0001). The findings establish a benign constitutional centromeric heteromorphism of chromosome 1 and highlight the importance of distinguishing such variants from structural chromosomal abnormalities during routine cytogenetic evaluation.

title: Fast and background-suppressed DNA-PAINT
authors: Sun, T.; Liu, S.; Zhang, X.; Tang, H.; Hua, B.; Xia, X.-H.
abstract: The speed and resolution of DNA-PAINT imaging is partly limited by the background fluorescence at high imager-strand concentrations. Here, we combine the photoactivatable fluorophore-quencher-DNA probes with the photoactivation, diffusion, and excitation strategy on a spinning disk confocal microscope, decoupling background fluorescence from the imager-strand concentration. This method yields >7-fold faster DNA-PAINT imaging in cells, a ~15 nm localization precision in hydrogels, without using specialized or speed-optimized imager strands.

title: Tycholyzer: NanoTemper NT.6 Tycho Analysis Tool
abstract: NanoTemper Tycho NT.6 is a nano differential scanning fluorimetry (nanoDSF) instrument that enables rapid measurement of apparent protein melting temperatures. Thermal shift assays are widely used to assess protein stability under different conditions, including screening for protein-ligand interactions. These experiments often involve multiple samples, conditions, and replicates collected across several instrument runs, generating datasets that can be cumbersome to organize, compare, and analyze quantitatively. Here, we introduce Tycholyzer, a user-friendly software application that streamlines processing and analysis of Tycho nanoDSF data. Tycholyzer allows users to combine data from multiple runs, inspect and select individual fluorescence traces, and normalize and group replicate profiles for comparison across experimental conditions. The software provides two complementary approaches for determining apparent melting temperatures: sigmoidal fitting of fluorescence ratio profiles and identification of extrema in their first derivatives. Automated fitting of individual replicates enables calculation of mean melting temperatures and standard deviations, facilitating quantitative assessment of experimental variability. By integrating these capabilities into a single graphical interface, Tycholyzer promotes consistent, efficient, and rigorous analysis of nanoDSF experiments. Tycholyzer is freely available and can be run in MATLAB or as a standalone application using MATLAB Runtime (https://github.com/VGhani/Tycholyzer.git).

title: EcoToxFred: A knowledge-graph-grounded conversational agent for exploring ecotoxicological monitoring and hazard data
authors: Scheibe, P.; Schmid, T. S.; Schor, J.
abstract: Assessing chemical risks to aquatic ecosystems requires the joint interpretation of monitoring data, ecotoxicity data, and derived risk indicators, yet such integrated data are rarely accessible to users without database expertise. We present EcoToxFred, an open-source conversational agent that provides natural language access to a curated knowledge graph of chemical monitoring and hazard data for European surface waters. EcoToxFred couples a large language model (LLM) with a Neo4j graph database in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) architecture. An agent interprets user questions, selects tools, translates questions into graph queries, and returns answers as text, tables, or interactive maps, together with the executed query for reproducibility. We evaluated EcoToxFred with GPT-4.1 and GPT-5 on a benchmark of 25 questions, including six questions derived from an expert workshop, each posed three times. Answers were scored for tool selection, execution accuracy against human-written reference queries, and goal accuracy using the RAGAS evaluation framework with an independent LLM judge. With both models, EcoToxFred selected an appropriate tool in at least 92% of runs and reproduced the reference result in 74% of runs with a reference query, including all lookup questions. Goal accuracy was 52% with GPT-4.1 and 63% with GPT-5. Failures concentrated on multi-step analytical questions, incomplete presentation of long results, and mismatches between user and database vocabulary. EcoToxFred shows how knowledge-graph-grounded LLM agents can lower the barrier to ecotoxicological data exploration while keeping answers traceable to the underlying data, and its architecture is transferable to other ecological data infrastructures.
